text.text_excerpt: Some of the best cupcakes in town! The chocolate with mint frosting, the coconut and the Oreo cupcakes are my favorites. They also have a great red velvet, it's just not my favorite one in town. Another good thing is that the cupcakes aren't gigantic. That seems to be the case with a lot of the trendier cupcake places (Crumbs). I'm addicted to their cupcakes and I've only had one that let me down: the Bananas Foster. The cake itself was too dense, heavy and dry for my taste, but I know that can happen when cooking with bananas so maybe it was just a bad batch. They also close relatively early on weekdays, but offer a great happy hour if you get there later in the day. Definitely, a perfec...

Like many others, I was turned onto Bee Sweet by the Living Social coupon and got 6 cupcakes for $7. I've had cupcakes from the Kupcake factory and I was so disappointed that I didn't have high hopes for Bee Sweet. Fortunately for them and for my massive sweet tooth, it was love at first bite for me and that delicious red velvet. It was definitely one of the best ones I've ever had ever. EVA. The cake was perfectly moist and it tasted slightly more choclatey than other red velvets I've had, but this made it so much better. The frosting was good too, but I've had better. I also got the strawberry, the chocolate oreo, the milk chocolate (?), and the chocolate with m&m's. The strawberry was ...

I've tried several cupcake/dessert places in the city and I have to say this is my favorite. The cupcakes aren't too dry and aren't too too sweet, which is saying a lot compared to other New Orleans' places. Try the PB&J one - it sounds really weird but the guy working there persuaded me to try one and I have to say that I want to go back and just get a pack of those. The red velvet is also good. (If you don't have a large sweet tooth, don't eat the flowers and other garnishments on top.)
